newsitem.title: CHINA: China newspaper dismisses inflation rise.
newsitem.headline: China newspaper dismisses inflation rise.

text.p: The official China Securities newspaper on Thursday shrugged off the impact of rising inflation in August, saying that Beijing could control inflation at around six percent for all this year.
"Although overall price levels rose in August, the range of the rebound was lower than expected," the newspaper said.
"Historical data show that August is always a month when prices rebound but this year's rise was lower than in the previous few years," it added.

The State Statistical Bureau on Tuesday said consumer price inflation rose by 1.5 percentage points from July to a year-on- year 8.1 percent in August in the first upturn since February this year, due to rising vegetable and meat prices.

The newspaper said that, because of the lower-than-expected rise in August, prices were likely to stabilise in September and October, making inflation for the whole of 1996 around six percent, compared with 14.8 percent last year.
It said the falling inflation was mainly due to an improvement in the national economy in 1996.
